utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Katic. I'll move to a different topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter 24327.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just correct the transcript. Line 21 the witness said: Or somewhere from the depth of the territory.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: This is a synonym of "from behind the lines."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's only a matter of the record. If the Prosecutor will kindly check whether this was indeed said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I was confirmed by the interpreters that "from behind the lines" is a synonym to that expression, but we note it. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, you'll recognise this photo as a photo that you marked in the Dragomir Milosevic case. Do you recognise the photo?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And can you confirm for us today that F is -- you marked F for the faculty of philosophy?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: M for the museum?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: HI for the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: B for the Metaljka building?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And the line that you drew on this photo was the separation line between the VRS above the line and the ABiH below the line; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I tender this as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 24327 receives number P6044, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You're going to ask some questions about this?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Katic, there were men with rifles on the upper floor of the Metaljka building and the building to its left on this map, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot see it on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter number 24328.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Katic, I'd like to remind you of your testimony in this -- on this issue in the Dragomir Milosevic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, the question was not whether you can see the men with rifles on this photo, whether you were aware -- the question was whether there were men with rifles on the upper floor of that building you marked.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the roof of that building there could have been no people. They could have been on lower floors or perhaps on the highest floor, but they couldn't be on the roof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It may be a translation issue. I didn't say so neither Ms. McKenna say so. The question was whether there were men with rifles on the upper floor of the building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, sir, there were armed people in that building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And from the positions from the upper floors of that building, these men could shoot down the street running from the Metaljka building towards the Holiday Inn to hit targets in front of the Holiday Inn if they choose to do so; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: If they wanted to, they could hit it from that building.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: So these men could effectively engage targets from the Metaljka building and the building to its left with or without a telescopic sight on their rifles, couldn't they?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Well, the distance is about 400 metres. They could without telescopic sights shoot.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, at statement -- or at paragraph 16 of your statement you refer to the red building which was divided between the VRS and the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Could we please see D2623.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Now, the red building to which you refer is the building marked with an S and an M in this photograph; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And at paragraph 10 of your statement you confirmed that the Serb forces were in the part marked S and Muslim forces in the part marked M; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: The whole area to the left of this building on the photo was held by the VRS, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: The area to the left of this building was under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And the area in front of the building, that's towards the Miljacka river on the photo, was also held by the VRS; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And the area behind the building was also held by the VRS; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: I did not understand this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'll be more clear. The area behind the building, so in the opposite direction to the Miljacka river, was also held by the VRS; is that correct? The area at the lower part of the photo.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: You mean left on the photograph? Is that what you mean? When I look at the photograph, the left side?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I mean the bottom part of the photograph, the bottom left. Mr. Katic, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: So just to simplify things, we can agree that the red building was almost entirely surrounded by VRS forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Not quite. Not completely. On the right-hand side on this picture there were forces of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you. At paragraph 16 of your statement you say: "It was possible to fire shots from this building on the area in front of the Holiday Inn, S curve area, to cause incidents. This means that Bosnian soldiers could have fired shots in order to cause incidents." And then you seem to backtrack somewhat from this statement and then you say: "Nonetheless some tall buildings and trees could obstruct the line of sight between the S curve area and the red building." Mr. Katic, I'd like you to examine this photo and examine the line of sight from the Muslim-held part of the red building to the Holiday Inn. And you'll agree that the first obstruction is the tall building to the left of the building marked 1 on the map. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: From the red building, regardless of whether it's marked with S or M, it was possible to shoot at Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Well, again, Mr. Katic --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. That's why I said in my previous statement that the building I marked as the Metaljka building was impossible for soldiers of the Army of Republika Srpska to occupy on the roof or the upper floors because of the possibility that soldiers from the red building marked with M could fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, I think we can agree that anybody standing on the roof of the red building or, indeed, the Metaljka building, would be exposed to fire from the opposite side. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And we can also agree that there was nothing preventing soldiers from taking positions in the upper floor of the Metaljka building, and as you already confirmed in your previous testimony there were, in fact, soldiers on the upper floor - correct - and as you confirmed today?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And now focusing on the red building, leaving aside the issue of the Metaljka building, focusing on the red building, I'd like you to examine the line of sight between the red building and the S curve area in front of the Holiday Inn -- in fact, perhaps if we look at this line of sight from a different perspective it may be even clearer to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Could we please see D2526.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we learn the date and time when the photograph was taken to be sure that everything we see on the picture existed then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we all know. Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Now, again, Mr. Katic, I'd like you to examine the line of sight -- if you can orientate yourself, can you see the red building in the top left-hand corner of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: I see the red building.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And again, I'd ask you to focus on the line of sight between the ABiH-held part of that building --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Ms. McKenna. Why don't you ask the witness to mark the red building on this photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, could you please mark the red building on this photo. The usher will assist you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, I think we'll have to go back to the previous photo so you can orientate yourself correctly. Would you like to make a correction?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we can -- you can delete your marking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I see red and then I see it's a new building.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: So just to clarify, the X you've placed is not on the smaller red building, but the larger longer building behind the small building; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: To be clearer, you may circle the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Katic, you could circle the ABiH-held part of the building.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, again focusing on the line of sight between that part of the building and the S curve area in front of the Holiday Inn - and we can zoom in on the buildings -- the tall building in front of the red building if it would be helpful, but you will agree that along that line of sight you first are obstructed by the tall building to the left of the Metaljka building on this photograph; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Would you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, an ABiH soldier shooting downwards from that part of the building held by the ABiH would be obstructed by the tall buildings in front of him on the VRS-held side of the Miljacka river; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: May I have an intervention. First I should know whether Mr. Katic speaks English or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, do you speak English?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: I don't speak English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you kindly take off your headphones for the moment. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe, Your Excellency -- [In English] Sorry, I have to speak in English. I believe, Excellencies, that those questions are misleading since Mr. Katic was not deployed in this area. All of those guesses and speculations --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: -- are not taking into account levels and trajectories and anything, just speculation that I can't recover during the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But, Mr. Karadzic, take a look at paragraph 16. Paragraph 16 the witness stated that it was possible to fire shots from this building on the area in front of Holiday Inn, S curve area, to cause incidents. So it's --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes, Excellency. But why we don't have -- why we don't have better photo? Because this photo is -- the angle is completely wrong and it can't be proven what --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, but then if it's -- you can re-examine the witness with more proper photo in your turn.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then let's continue. Mr. Katic, I hope you understand my body language. Yes, thank you. That can't express my gesture. Yes, let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may briefly examine the record. Your Honour, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we ask the witness to date and sign this photo?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you for the reminder, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, could you please date and sign this photo in the bottom corner.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: And if I may tender this, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number P6045, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Katic, first of all, was your battalion deployed here in this area?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Our battalion was not deployed in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where was your battalion deployed and how far is that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Our battalion was deployed in the sector overlooking Debelo Brdo via Zlatiste up to Osmice on the road towards Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we clarify what "your battalion" or "our battalion" means. When he was serving as a battalion member or when he was the president of Novo Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you were in the army, according to what is stated in paragraph -- up to 13 March, where were you deployed until 13 March?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: I said a moment ago when I said "our battalion," that's the battalion where I was up to 13 March in the Army of Republika Srpska, in the sector. From Debelo Brdo via Zlatiste, up to Osmice, on the road leading to Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Katic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now call up 65 ter 21215, a photograph from another vantage point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you, first of all, mark the buildings where the Muslim army had positions or controlled, which other buildings did they control, apart from the red one, on the left side of the Miljacka river -- or even better, could you mark the buildings they controlled as well as the part of the area at Brdo they controlled?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Shall I draw the separation line as it was during the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, do draw that line.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: To the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did that line go between the buildings uphill?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did go uphill, towards the top, towards the Jewish cemetery, which is at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you write an S on the left-hand side and M on the right-hand side in Latinic script.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there optical visibility from these positions on the mountaintops in terms of the part of the road that was in front of the Holiday Inn hotel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, you're -- yes, Ms. McKenna.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is outside the scope of the cross-examination, which was focused simply on the line of visibility from the ABiH-held part of the red building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't think the cross-examination can be construed that narrowly. The issue is if someone was sniped on in front of the Holiday Inn, which side was it coming from, so I don't think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But take a look at paragraph 16 of the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen paragraph 16 but does that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It deals with exclusively red building.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it does but does that -- we're not limited by that. If he wants to say -- if the implication is that there's no way that the Muslims could have shot someone in front of that Holiday Inn building, then Dr. Karadzic is entitled to show they could have shot from all kinds of places. He's not limited to the red building to rebut that inference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, just a second. Interpretation has only now been completed. Yes, Ms. McKenna.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honour, the cross-examination was limited solely to the issue of the possibility of -- the witness's contention was that there was a line of sight between the ABiH-held part of the red building and the S curve in front of the Holiday Inn. That was the sole topic of the cross-examination, and anything broader than that does not stem from the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I believe that Ms. McKenna also asked on this picture to tell -- for him to tell where the Serbs were and where the Muslims were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, I think we have heard enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the relevance of the issue, we would allow the accused to pose the questions. But if necessary, we would also allow the Prosecution to put further questions if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry, I'd like to raise a slightly broader point. This may not -- about this kind of statement followed by these kinds of questions on re-direct. This may not be the moment to do it but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I would not entertain your submission. Why don't we proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. But I'd like to reserve the opportunity to do so, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, Madam McKenna asked you about these buildings behind the red building to the south, who they belonged to. Did you mark it in the following way now that part of these buildings that went uphill belonged to the Muslim side and another part belonged to the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From this point of view do you know or do you believe that there is visibility between this vantage point and the red building and the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Now that I look at this photograph, I see a building here which is taller than the red building. Probably it was built later in peace time. Optically speaking, one could not fire from the red building now that I'm looking at the location in front of the Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could one fire from these high areas close to the Jewish cemetery? Could one fire at this section of the road?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were asked whether any Serb soldiers could have been on the higher floors of Metaljka. You said that that was possible but that then they would have been under threat. I'm not asking you whether that was possible. I'm asking you whether there actually were soldiers up there on the higher floors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you answer, Mr. Katic. Yes, Ms. McKenna.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: This question was asked and answered. The witness already confirmed that there were soldiers on the upper floors of the Metaljka building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with Ms. McKenna.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The answer wasn't given to me, Excellency. The answer was given to the OTP, that it was -- that it could have happened. But I'm asking in re-direct now not only whether that could have been happened, but I'm asking whether he saw from the front line that there actually were soldiers up on those higher floors. So I'm actually changing my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you at the front line as a soldier and did you see soldiers on these higher floors?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: From which army, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Serb army? I'm talking about Metaljka, the Metaljka building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood. I understood the question. I was never as a soldier on this position and, and, there is this reality. Soldiers were everywhere on first floors or in basements at the front line to guard their positions. But I did not claim then that they could have climbed the roof or these higher floors. I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that on higher floors --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I -- proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that on higher floors they could have been under threat from the red building. Could they have been under threat from some facility on the right bank of the Miljacka that was under the control of the Muslim forces, and can you tell us which buildings existed from which one could fire at Metaljka?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: All the buildings on the right bank of the Miljacka river - well, not all of them but most of them - are taller than the Assembly building, the Holiday Inn building, and over here the well-known Unis buildings that were called Momo and Uzeir, that's what we called them. All of these were more dominant in relation to the Metaljka building, that is, on the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were asked whether they could shoot. Do you have any information to the effect that Serb soldiers intentionally fired at the area in front of the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: I do not have any information of the Serb soldiers ever intentionally shooting at civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I kindly ask you to place the date and your initials on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D2655, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, in one of the questions -- in one of the answers you gave to Mr. Karadzic's question you stated - it's transcript page 61, line 24 and on: I understood the question: "I was never as a soldier on this position and there is this reality," you're talking about this red building or Metaljka -- oh, yes, Metaljka building. "Soldiers were everywhere on first floors or in basements at the front line to guard their position, but I did not claim then that they could have climbed the roof or these higher floors. I did not see them." So I'm not sure if there's a translation issue, but I limit my question to the case related to the higher floors -- rooms located in higher floors, be it sixth floor, seventh floor, or fifth floor. I'm not meaning the roof. In your earlier answer to the question posed by Ms. McKenna you stated that, and I -- it is after my intervention, you confirmed that there were armed people in that building in the -- on the upper floor of that building --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, are you reading from transcript 49 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- lines 21 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: But he says "could," there could have been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no, I will read out my question. The question was -- this is what I said -- it's line 25 of transcript 49. The question was whether there were men with rifles on the upper floor of that building." And witness's answer: "Judge, sir, there were armed people in that building." So you confirmed that there were armed people on the upper floor of that Metaljka building, and now you are claiming that you didn't see the armed men. So what was your basis in confirming that there were armed people on the upper floor of Metaljka building, Mr. Katic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let me tell you. In these buildings, not all the tenants were moved out. In some buildings there were families that lived there. It is possible that on some floor a family had stayed behind with two soldiers who lived there and could have weapons and did have weapons in their apartment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Katic. I'll leave it at that. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In terms of continuity with this question put by His Excellency, Mr. Kwon, can you tell us from your own experience whether people fired from buildings where their families were; and if so, what were the reasons?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: They certainly did not fire from their apartments, these soldiers who lived in these apartments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For what reason?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Well, because this was not the place. He had a particular military place where he went to this -- to defend this military line that had been taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. For planning purposes, do you have many questions more?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five or six minutes, Excellency. Five minutes, whatever you prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to have further cross-examination, Ms. McKenna?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: At this stage, no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then shall we continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we briefly take a look at D2623. And could Mr. Katic please be assisted as he uses the pen -- I paper P6044. It's a Prosecution document, 6044. Can it be enlarged a bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, what is under this red line that you drew?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: Underneath the red line is the Miljacka river.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you the following: Do you see this curve, S, on the road right in front of the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this being zoomed in a bit more? All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It seems that the vehicles stopped at the traffic light. Do you see this S line where the tram moves from one side to the other?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be zoomed in a bit more now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see it now, Mr. Katic, on the road itself?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: I see --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see where the tram forks off and moves to the right-hand side towards the faculty, do you see that S curve?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: I see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you draw a line on this S curve.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please draw a line for us along the pavement on the street called Rackog, can you cut across this curve. Yes, yes, just go on that way.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I kindly ask you to place the date there and your initials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see the point of these markings, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellency, it can be seen clearly that the point is that the faculty shields the S curve and that from the S curve one cannot fire from Metaljka. I can't put that question as well, but I just wanted someone who was from the area to mark these relations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then if that was the point we need to have these markings in a not-zoomed big photo. So could we ask the witness to mark these -- make these markings again on the original one now that he understood where the S mark is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I kindly ask you, Mr. Katic, to now draw the same line, these same two lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is he able to mark now? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your opinion, can something on this curve be hit from Metaljka?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: From Metaljka here on the road, the S curve, the tram cannot be hit because the faculty building is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now place the date and your initials there.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just one more question, Mr. Katic. As president of the municipality you knew what the powers of the municipality were and the domain of defence. The municipality and local communes, did they have their own organisations of Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC
utterances.text: They had a defence department, not local communes, but the municipality did have a defence department.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the Territorial Defence, how was it regulated in that system of ours? Companies, the municipality, local communes, did they have their Territorial Defences and where did they keep their weapons?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I tender this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You have been asked about the provenance of weapons when the war broke out and you said they came from the JNA barracks. Was there any relationship between the JNA and the TO and did TO units have their own weapons?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Katic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be Exhibit D2656. Then that concludes your evidence, Mr. Katic -- I'm sorry, I didn't ask you, Ms. McKenna, no --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- re-cross. Thank you. So I thank you, Mr. Katic, for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go. But we'll rise all together and we'll have a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
